title: Pre-Market Briefing - 2026-07-31
markdown:
# Pre-Market Briefing

## 1. Market Tone
- **Risk-on/opening firm**: Thursday’s market showed strong gains across major indices, with the S&P 500 **7,438** (+1.66%), Nasdaq **25,122** (+2.78%), and Dow **52,208** (+1.19%) (The Motley Fool).
- **Post-earnings dispersion is high**: big gaps are being driven by whether companies showed “proof” of growth vs. only spending/expectations (The Motley Fool).

## 2. Macro And Calendar
- No formal macro calendar items or scheduled economic releases were provided in the email sources.
- The main pre-market driver is **earnings and guidance reaction** rather than macro data (The Motley Fool).

## 3. Earnings And Company News
- **Amazon (AMZN)**: reported revenue growth of **20% YoY** and AWS posted its fastest growth in **18 quarters**; stock was up over **10% pre-market** (The Motley Fool).
- **Apple (AAPL)**: revenue expectations for the coming quarter **missed consensus** and margin outlook was hit by supply-chain issues; stock was down around **7%** pre-market (The Motley Fool).
- **Tesla (TSLA)**: Elon Musk denied a WSJ report about advisers discussing a spin-off/sale/closure of the China unit in connection with a possible Tesla/SpaceX merger; stock had been up over **4%** pre-open on speculation, then gave back gains after the denial (The Motley Fool).
- **Roblox (RBLX)**: bookings grew **8% to $1.6B**, slower than **70%** growth in Q3 2025; stock fell over **14%** pre-market (The Motley Fool).
- **GoDaddy (GDDY)**: slight beat on revenue and earnings, but forward growth and outlook were viewed as unexciting; stock was down around **8%** pre-market (The Motley Fool).
- **Reddit (RDDT)**: beat earnings expectations, revenue was **$805M** and up more than **60% YoY** for the eighth straight quarter, but “search referrals were choppy”; stock was down around **10%** pre-market (The Motley Fool).
- **Chevron (CVX)**: reported record U.S. production volumes, up **20%** from last year, and signed an agreement to develop a power facility in West Texas providing capacity to Microsoft; stock was up around **3%** pre-open (The Motley Fool).
- **Cboe Global Markets (CBOE)**: expected to post double-digit revenue and earnings growth this quarter; management will be watched for another possible full-year guide raise (The Motley Fool).
- **T. Rowe Price (TROW)**: expected to benefit from higher advisory fees and AUM, but outflows, fee pressure, and expenses remain key questions (The Motley Fool).
- **Moderna (MRNA)**: earnings today; focus is on whether non-COVID respiratory pipeline progress can build a durable franchise (The Motley Fool).

## 4. Top Movers And Catalysts
- **AMZN**: strongest mover on cloud growth acceleration and “proof” of monetization from prior spending.
- **AAPL**: weakness tied to margin pressure and supply-chain concerns.
- **RBLX**: sharp downside on slowing bookings growth; key concern is monetization/retention.
- **RDDT**: down on user-acquisition concern despite strong revenue growth.
- **GDDY**: lower on cautious outlook and AI-transition uncertainty.
- **CVX**: higher on production growth and a Microsoft-linked power project.
- **TSLA**: news-driven volatility, but the main report was denied by Musk.

## 5. Ranked Buy Candidates
1. **AMZN**
   - **Catalyst**: 20% revenue growth and AWS fastest growth in 18 quarters; market is rewarding “proof” of conversion.
   - **Why it matters for a swing trade**: a major earnings gap with clear fundamental surprise can attract momentum buyers and follow-through.
   - **What invalidates it**: if the gap fails to hold, the post-earnings move is quickly sold, or guidance/details do not support the headline strength.
   - **Check before entry**: opening range behavior, whether pre-market gains are holding, and any guidance/segment detail confirming the AWS acceleration.

2. **CVX**
   - **Catalyst**: record U.S. production volumes, up 20%, plus a West Texas power facility agreement supporting Microsoft capacity.
   - **Why it matters for a swing trade**: positive operational surprise plus a strategic project can support a short-term rerating in an energy name.
   - **What invalidates it**: if the market ignores the production beat or the move fades on broader oil/energy weakness.
   - **Check before entry**: whether the stock holds the early gain and whether traders are valuing the Microsoft-linked project as material or just a side note.

3. **CBOE**
   - **Catalyst**: expected double-digit growth in both revenue and earnings; possible another full-year guidance raise.
   - **Why it matters for a swing trade**: if delivered, this is the type of quality earnings setup that can extend on continued volume strength.
   - **What invalidates it**: if results/guidance merely meet expectations without an upside revision, implying normalization.
   - **Check before entry**: actual earnings release, guidance tone, and whether elevated trading volumes are sustained.

4. **MRNA**
   - **Catalyst**: earnings today with the market focused on the respiratory pipeline beyond COVID.
   - **Why it matters for a swing trade**: any evidence of durable pipeline momentum could reframe the story.
   - **What invalidates it**: if the update confirms the business is still overly dependent on declining COVID revenue.
   - **Check before entry**: actual print, pipeline commentary, and whether the quarter supports a diversified growth narrative.

## 6. Swing Setup Board
- **AMZN** — **Catalyst Continuation**
  - **Trigger**: hold early breakout / opening range above the pre-market gap.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: lose the gap and fail to reclaim it.
  - **First target logic**: look for continuation only if breadth and volume support follow-through after the open.
  - **Sizing caution**: gap-up earnings names can be volatile; size smaller if chasing.
  - **Pass if**: the open is a gap-and-fade or the move is already extended before entry.

- **CVX** — **Breakout / Momentum**
  - **Trigger**: constructive hold above the pre-market bid and continuation after the open.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: give back the early post-earnings gain.
  - **First target logic**: first push is likely toward prior swing resistance or a measured follow-through from the earnings gap.
  - **Sizing caution**: energy can reverse with commodity sentiment; avoid oversized entries on headline-only strength.
  - **Pass if**: the market treats the beat as already priced in.

- **RBLX** — **Risk Watch**
  - **Trigger**: only consider if it stabilizes after a major gap down and reclaims key intraday levels.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: any failure to stabilize after the opening flush.
  - **First target logic**: bounce traders would need confirmation that the selloff was overdone relative to the rest of the report.
  - **Sizing caution**: very high volatility; not ideal for aggressive sizing.
  - **Pass if**: the market continues to price in slowing monetization and retention concerns.

- **RDDT** — **Reversal Bounce**
  - **Trigger**: watch for an intraday washout followed by reclaim of the opening range.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: inability to hold above the rebound pivot.
  - **First target logic**: a relief move would need to come from the strong revenue growth offsetting the search-referral concern.
  - **Sizing caution**: headline risk is high because the issue is about user acquisition durability.
  - **Pass if**: search-referral weakness dominates and the stock cannot stabilize.

- **GDDY** — **Risk Watch**
  - **Trigger**: only if the market decides the AI transition is more credible than the cautious outlook suggests.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: continued selling after the open.
  - **First target logic**: any bounce would likely be technical, not thesis-changing.
  - **Sizing caution**: weak post-earnings tone; not an obvious long setup.
  - **Pass if**: you need to assume fast fundamental reacceleration without evidence.

- **AAPL** — **Risk Watch**
  - **Trigger**: wait for a clear stabilization signal; no strong buy setup is provided in the source.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: continued margin-pressure narrative and supply-chain concern.
  - **First target logic**: only a technical rebound unless the company later clarifies the margin hit.
  - **Sizing caution**: heavy pre-market gap lower can remain pressured.
  - **Pass if**: the supply-chain/margin issue remains unresolved.

- **TSLA** — **Risk Watch**
  - **Trigger**: only if the market re-focuses on fundamentals rather than the denied report.
  - **Stop / invalidation**: renewed speculation or conflicting filing/reporting.
  - **First target logic**: any move would be news-driven and likely headline-sensitive.
  - **Sizing caution**: do not anchor on the denied merger/spin-off rumor alone.
  - **Pass if**: the trade is based solely on social-media denial rather than verified filings.

## 7. Setup Watch
- **AMZN**: strongest active long candidate from the provided material.
- **CVX**: secondary long candidate if early strength holds.
- **CBOE**: watch for actual earnings/guidance confirmation before considering a trade.
- **MRNA**: only actionable if the earnings update gives a clearer pipeline catalyst.
- **RDDT**: watch for a reflex bounce, but only as a tactical reversal attempt.
- **RBLX**: watch for stabilization; otherwise avoid catching a falling knife.
- **AAPL**: monitor for whether the gap lower turns into a tradable oversold bounce or continues lower.

## 8. Risk Watch
- **AAPL**: supply-chain and margin pressure could keep the stock under pressure.
- **RBLX**: bookings slowdown raises monetization/retention concerns.
- **RDDT**: dependence on search referrals is a clear risk to the bull case.
- **GDDY**: cautious outlook may limit upside even after a beat.
- **TSLA**: rumor-driven volatility; source material says the report was denied, but confirmation risk remains.
- **MRNA**: earnings risk remains high because the market is looking for evidence of a durable non-COVID franchise.

## 9. Sector And Theme Watch
- **Cloud / AI infrastructure**: AMZN’s AWS acceleration is the clearest confirmation of “proof” being rewarded (The Motley Fool).
- **Consumer tech / platform monetization**: RBLX and RDDT both show concern around whether engagement translates into durable monetization.
- **Energy / integrateds**: CVX strength reflects production growth and strategic infrastructure linkage.
- **Market volume / volatility**: CBOE may benefit if elevated trading activity continues.
- **Pharma / respiratory pipeline**: MRNA remains a pipeline story more than a COVID-only story.
- **Supply chain / hardware margins**: AAPL highlights margin pressure from memory chips and supplier constraints.

## 10. Worth Reading
- “**Amazon Cloud Growth Trumps Apple Margin Hit**” — useful for framing the market’s current preference for earnings proof over spending promises (The Motley Fool).
- “**Musk Denies WSJ Report on Tesla-SpaceX**” — useful only to understand why TSLA was volatile; verify with filings or follow-up reporting before acting (The Motley Fool).
- “**After-Hours Fireworks From Team Rule Breakers Recs**” — the RBLX, GDDY, and RDDT reactions summarize the main post-earnings debate points (The Motley Fool).
- “**Four to Watch on Friday AM: CVX, MRNA, TROW, CBOE**” — provides the cleanest list of names to monitor into the open (The Motley Fool).

## 11. Open Questions
- Will **AMZN** hold its pre-market gain once regular-session liquidity hits?
- Is **AAPL**’s margin/supply-chain issue a one-quarter problem or a bigger trend?
- Was **RBLX**’s bookings slowdown a one-off, or a real monetization/retention inflection?
- Can **RDDT** keep growing revenue strongly if search referrals remain choppy?
- Does **CVX**’s production beat translate into follow-through buying, or is it already priced in?
- Will **MRNA** show evidence that the non-COVID pipeline is becoming a durable growth engine?
- Can **CBOE** extend if management raises guidance again, or is growth normalizing?

### Notable Noise
- The retirement-planning content and broader motivational commentary are not actionable for the trading open.
- The **TSLA** rumor discussion is low-confidence until confirmed by filings or reliable follow-up reporting.
- **TROW** is mentioned only as an expectations item; no concrete earnings result was provided in the source material.
